access_policy: Offer each support independently to everyone. Teacher/SLSO may demonstrate it; do not assign diagnostic modes or fixed tiers.

guided_strip.label: Find a clue
guided_strip.instruction: Read or listen to one location detail. Point to the detail you want to use.

guided_strip.label: Match an action
guided_strip.instruction: Choose two possible actions. Find their numbers for this location.

guided_strip.label: Explain
guided_strip.instruction: Say, show or note why one action fits and what it might miss or depend on.

number_support.instruction: Read the selected effect at each location. Add those three numbers once.
number_support.example_rule: Show an expression from the learner’s actual arrangement. Never insert the highest-total arrangement as the default.
number_support.incomplete_total_label: So far — choose all three locations for a complete total
number_support.remaining_policy: Optional extra detail: 300 minus the complete plan total. Do not make subtraction a new core requirement.
number_support.tile_policy: Provide labelled location/effect tiles for print and the same labels on screen. Automatic calculation does not select an action.

reasoning_prompts: Which location detail supports this action?
Which rubbish might this action miss?
What needs to keep happening for this action to work?
What changes if you move this action to another location?
comparison_prompts: What is the same in your two plans? What is different?
Which plan has the larger simulated reduction?
What do you gain or give up with that plan?
Which location clue helps explain your preference?
frames: This action fits ___ because the description says ___.
At ___, this action reduces ___ pieces in the simulation.
collaboration_prompts: Would you like to share a clue, a choice or a concern?
I build on that idea because ___.
I see it differently because the description says ___.
How did that idea affect our plan?
depth_prompts: Could you defend a plan with a smaller numerical reduction?
What extra information would help you decide?
Which part of your recommendation is certain in the simulation, and which part is your judgment?
comparison_row_fields: What it might miss or depend on
focus_mode: Show one location’s key points and the same location column for two learner-selected actions. Restore all information at any time. Never replace full content with a permanently reduced task.
guardrails: In Explore/Test screens, prompts do not supply completed action-specific limitations.
Show worked solutions and limitations on the separate Answers for the teacher screen; do not automatically recommend or score them within Test your plan.
No reward, timer, ranking or diagnostic labels.
Do not make speaking, handwriting or dragging compulsory.
Group comparison scaffolds are not the separate individual exit slip.
